entities.summary: Armand Séguin (1869–1903) was a post-Impressionist French painter who is remembered for his involvement in the Pont-Aven School beginning in 1891. In 1892, he returned to Pont-Aven where he met Renoir and Émile Bernard. The following year, he associated with Paul Gauguin, who gave him lessons, and collaborated with Roderic O'Conor in producing etchings. Armand Seguin was a painters & sculptors from Paris (1869-04-15, Paris–1903-12-30). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.
